faq.q: What are the symptoms of ear mites in dogs?
faq.a: Head shaking, constant ear scratching and dark brown, dry or crusty debris that looks like coffee grounds. Heavy cases can cause scabs around the ear, a swollen ear flap or an ear infection.

faq.q: How can I tell ear mites from an ear infection?
faq.a: Not by looking: dark discharge also appears with yeast and bacterial infections. A vet confirms mites with an otoscope or by checking a sample of ear debris under the microscope.

faq.q: What is the best home remedy for ear mites in dogs?
faq.a: Home remedies aren't recommended. The Merck Veterinary Manual advises against irritating mixtures such as vinegar because they can worsen inflammation. Vet-prescribed anti-parasite products, plus ear cleaning, are what clear ear mites.

faq.q: Are ear mites contagious to humans?
faq.a: Rarely. At most they may cause a temporary itchy rash in some people, which clears once the pets are treated. They spread easily between dogs and cats, so all pets in the home should be treated.

faq.q: Can dogs get ear mites from cats?
faq.a: Yes. Ear mites pass between cats and dogs by close contact, and cats can carry them without symptoms. Treat every animal in the household at the same time.
